item.title: Police arrest suspect over railway vandalism in Ogun, recover 16 iron rods
item.description: By James Ogunnaike Abeokuta The Ogun State Police Command has arrested a 36-year-old man, Shobande Taofeek, over alleged vandalism and theft of railway infrastructure in the Arigbajo area of the state. The police also recovered 16 railway iron rods and two gas cylinders suspected to have been stolen during the operation. The arrest was carried out by operatives of the Special Weapons and Tactics (SWAT) unit of the command following intelligence reports about the alleged vandalism and theft of railway materials in the area. In a statement issued on Sunday, the Police Public Relations Officer, Ogun State Command, DSP Oluseyi Babaseyi, said the operatives intensified surveillance and patrols in the affected area on Friday October 23, leading to the suspect’s arrest. According to the statement, the suspect subsequently led the operatives to an uncompleted building where the recovered items were found. “On 23 October 2026, SWAT operatives intensified surveillance and patrols in the affected area, leading to the suspect’s arrest. He subsequently led the operatives to an uncompleted building where the stolen items were recovered as exhibits,” the statement said. The police further disclosed that preliminary investigations indicated that the suspect had allegedly admitted involvement in similar offences on three previous occasions. However, the command said investigations were ongoing to establish the full circumstances surrounding the alleged crime and identify other individuals who might have been involved. “Efforts are ongoing to apprehend other suspects connected with the crime and recover any additional stolen property,” the statement added. The State Commissioner of Police, Bode Ojajuni, reiterated the command’s commitment to protecting public assets and critical infrastructure, warning that those responsible for vandalism would be brought to justice. Ojajuni, according to the statement, reaffirmed the command’s “unwavering commitment to protecting public assets, safeguarding critical infrastructure and bringing perpetrators of economic sabotage to justice.” He also called on residents to support security agencies by providing credible and timely information that could help prevent crime and protect public infrastructure across the state. The police urged members of the public to cooperate with law enforcement agencies, stressing the importance of community participation in crime prevention and the maintenance of safer communities. item.title: Real Madrid’s Courtois to miss El Classico due to illness
item.description: Real Madrid have suffered a major setback ahead of their El Clasico clash against Barcelona after goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois was ruled out of Sunday’s La Liga encounter due to illness. The Belgian goalkeeper has contracted the flu and will miss the Matchday 10 fixture at Camp Nou, forcing Madrid to turn to Ukrainian shot-stopper Andriy Lunin. The development comes at a crucial time for Real Madrid, who trail Barcelona by six points in the La Liga standings and need a positive result to strengthen their title challenge. Real Madrid confirmed Courtois’ late withdrawal in a statement released hours before kick-off. “Courtois is a last-minute withdrawal from tonight’s LaLiga matchday 10 game between Real Madrid and Barcelona due to a bout of the flu,” the club said. “Illia Voloshyn has been called up to the squad in his place.” Courtois’ absence represents a significant blow for Madrid, given his importance to the team and his recent performances. The 34-year-old was in action during Madrid’s recent Champions League outing, in which the club reportedly secured a 4-1 victory over RB Leipzig. His late withdrawal leaves Lunin with the responsibility of guarding Madrid’s goal in one of the most important fixtures of the season. Lunin is expected to start in goal in place of Courtois as Madrid prepare to face their fierce rivals. The 27-year-old has served as Courtois’ deputy in recent seasons and gained valuable experience during Madrid’s run to the Champions League final in 2024. He will now face a major test against a Barcelona side that has enjoyed an impressive start to the domestic campaign. Barcelona head into the encounter looking to maintain their strong league form, while Madrid will be eager to close the gap at the top of the standings. Madrid’s preparations have been further complicated by the absence of forward Vinícius Júnior, who remains unavailable as he serves a four-match domestic suspension. The Brazilian’s absence deprives Madrid of an important attacking option for the high-profile encounter. Madrid have also suffered two league defeats this season, against Real Betis and Atletico Madrid, increasing the pressure on the team to secure a result against Barcelona. With Courtois ruled out at the last minute and Vinícius unavailable, Madrid face a difficult challenge as they seek to reduce Barcelona’s six-point advantage in the La Liga title race. item.title: Taraba Govt mobilizes emergency relief, food supplies to Binnari after bandit attack
item.description: By Femi Bolaji JALINGO — The Taraba State Government has deployed emergency relief materials to Binnari community in Karim Lamido Local Government Area, less than 24 hours after a deadly bandit raid left more than forty residents dead and several households displaced. The rapid humanitarian intervention was executed on the direct directive of Governor Agbu Kefas, who mandated immediate state assistance to cushion the hardships faced by survivors of the Friday afternoon incursion. A high-powered government delegation led by the Executive Secretary of the Taraba State Emergency Management Agency (TSEMA), Dr. Audu Echuseh, arrived in the community on Saturday to coordinate the distribution of relief items and assess the extent of property destruction. The assessment team included the members representing Karim Lamido Constituencies at the Taraba State House of Assembly, Hon. Anas Shuaibu Didango and Hon. Abner Shittu; the Vice Chairman of Karim Lamido Local Government Council, Alhaji Uba Munyarda; alongside traditional rulers and community stakeholders. Addressing grieving residents during the distribution of supplies which included food grains, mattresses, blankets, and essential non-food items, Dr. Echuseh conveyed Governor Kefas’s deepest condolences to the bereaved families. She stated: “We are here on behalf of the Taraba State Government to show solidarity and provide immediate succour to our brothers and sisters in Binnari. His Excellency has directed that no victim of this dastardly act be left unattended to. “This is just the first phase of our intervention. The government is fully committed to providing necessary humanitarian support while collaborating with security agencies to ensure long-term stability and security in the area.” Reacting to the prompt response, the lawmakers commended the state government for its swift action, pledging total grassroots cooperation with security formations deployed to comb the area and forestall future attacks. Although the police claimed ten persons were killed, residents of the community said more than forty residents were lost to the attack. item.title: ‘My daughter, my biggest priority’ – Naomi Osaka considers quitting tennis
item.description: Former world number one Naomi Osaka cast doubt on her future Sunday saying she would consider quitting tennis if her three-year-old daughter asked her to. The four-time Grand Slam champion from Japan took 15 months away from the sport after the birth of her daughter Shai, before returning in 2023. She is in Tokyo to play at the Pan Pacific Open this week and said becoming a mother had reshaped her priorities. “I wouldn’t say I’m part-timing it but my entire day doesn’t consist of that,” said the 29-year-old, now ranked 19 in the world. “It’s tough, sometimes I look towards my future and I often wonder how long I’m going to play. “Because if my daughter did say she didn’t want me to travel as much, I’m not the type of person to ignore that.” Osaka also stepped away from tennis in 2021 to prioritise her mental health. She said her “mindset is changing a lot” with age. “My daughter is my biggest priority,” she said. “I try my best to put as much energy as I can into tennis. “If I think about it in certain ways, I’m really proud of where I am now because it’s not like I can dedicate my entire time to the sport.” – Online abuse – Osaka said juggling her duties as a player and a mother was something she was “figuring out little by little”. She also offered support to the American Coco Gauff, who said she had received an “insane” amount of racist abuse on the internet at this month’s China Open. World number five Gauff, who is Black, said the experience had been “kind of draining”. Osaka, whose mother is Japanese and father from Haiti, said “nobody should have to go through that”. “It’s sad but I’m used to it on my end,” she said. “I feel like for me, I’ve dealt with that my entire career through decisions that I make that seem to make some people upset. It’s tough.” Osaka said efforts made by women’s tennis governing body the WTA to combat social media abuse did not “ever seem to fully work all the way”. “I know that some people are like, OK, if it bothers you that much, stay off social media,” said Osaka. “But sometimes that’s the best way to connect with your fans. “From my end, what I do about it is I don’t really go on social media at all.” Osaka is seeded seven in Tokyo and plays Italy’s Jasmine Paolini in the first round. World number one Elena Rybakina of Kazakhstan and Philippines sensation Alexandra Eala are also competing. Osaka said she was “not far off” refinding her best form and was “optimistic for next year”. item.title: 2027: Tinubu has lost touch with reality, unaware he’s president — Shaibu
item.description: The Director of Strategic Communication of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) Presidential Campaign Council, Phrank Shaibu, has accused President Bola Tinubu of losing touch with reality, alleging that he is disconnected from the economic hardship facing Nigerians. Shaibu made the allegation during an interview on ARISE News on Sunday, faulting the president for blaming the opposition for hunger despite spending three and a half years in office. “He has lost touch with reality. Bola is not aware of his environment. He is not aware of what Nigerians are going through. He’s not even aware that he’s president,” Shaibu said. He described Tinubu’s explanation of the country’s hunger crisis as delusional, arguing that the president should take responsibility for the economic situation under his administration. “I watched him yesterday and my eight-year-old son who was beside me said, what’s this man talking about? He has been in office for three and a half years. And he’s talking about hunger being created by the opposition. I think it is delusional,” he said. Shaibu challenged Tinubu to compare the cost of living when he assumed office on May 29, 2023, with the current situation, arguing that Nigerians should not be worse off under his leadership. He cited the removal of petrol subsidy as a major factor behind rising prices, saying the policy triggered sharp increases in the cost of goods and services. “Bola Tinubu claimed the podium, and announced that subsidy was gone. And boom, what happened? Everything rose astronomically. The Nigerians cannot afford three square meals today,” he said. The ADC campaign official also alleged that higher university fees had forced some students out of school, despite the establishment of the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND). He further criticised Tinubu for continuing to blame the opposition, noting that the All Progressives Congress governed the country for eight years under former President Muhammadu Buhari before handing over power in 2023. Shaibu said Tinubu’s remarks on hunger raised questions about his understanding of the hardship experienced by ordinary Nigerians. He argued that the president should be held accountable for his administration’s economic policies rather than attributing the crisis to political opponents. For professionals and skilled workers, a valid national driver’s licence will be an added advantage. Applicants must also demonstrate good character and integrity. How to apply for EFCC recruitment 2026 Interested and qualified Nigerians are required to complete their applications online through the official EFCC recruitment portal. Follow these steps: Visit the official recruitment portal at https://recruitment.efcc.gov.ng . Review the available positions and select the category that matches your qualifications. Read the eligibility requirements carefully to confirm that you meet the criteria. Complete the online application form with accurate personal, educational and professional information. Declare all required academic and professional qualifications and provide the requested supporting information. Review your application to ensure that the details supplied are correct before submitting it. EFCC recruitment 2026: Deadline and application fee The recruitment information states that applications are expected to be submitted within one week of the commencement of the exercise. However, applicants should confirm the official opening and closing dates on the EFCC recruitment portal before submitting their applications, as a specific deadline was not provided in the supplied information. The application process is stated to be free of charge . Applicants are warned against individuals or organisations demanding money in exchange for recruitment assistance. The commission advises prospective candidates to rely on information published through its official recruitment portal and avoid unauthorised agents claiming to facilitate employment. item.title: 2027: Engaging APC data boys, insult to my integrity — Pat Utomi
item.description: A chieftain of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Professor Pat Utomi, has described engaging social media users he accused of being All Progressives Congress (APC) supporters paid to troll critics as an insult to his integrity. Utomi said the users began attacking him after he raised concerns about the living and working conditions of Nigerian soldiers, whom he said were poorly paid despite risking their lives to protect the country. In a post on X on Sunday, the economist alleged that some of those who criticised him were APC supporters benefiting from what he described as “stomach infrastructure”. “Yesterday, we talked about the poor living and working conditions of Nigerian soldiers compared to their counterparts in the US, and how senators are fattening their pockets with billions of naira while the soldiers who risk their lives every day to protect us are underpaid heavily,” he wrote. He said some social media users attacked him after he raised the issue, prompting him to examine their profiles. “Then, some fellows benefiting from stomach infrastructure began to bash us. I took a quick look at their profiles, and it became obvious to me that they were APC data boys trolling anyone who dared to speak up,” Utomi said. He added that he would not engage with the accounts, saying, “Engaging with any of them is an insult to my integrity.” In a separate post, Utomi also accused APC politicians of attempting to intimidate Nigerians ahead of the 2027 general election. He said Nigerians should not allow such actions to discourage them from participating in the electoral process. “We have seen videos of APC politicians trying to intimidate Nigerians ahead of the 2027 general elections,” he wrote. Utomi urged Nigerians to unite and resist what he described as attempts to instil fear ahead of the polls. “Nigerians need to understand that these fellows are powerless when we stand united. Do not allow them to sow seeds of fear in you,” he said. He also called on voters to participate in the election and protect the integrity of their votes. “Come out, vote, and defend your votes,” Utomi added. item.title: 1,314 protesters arrested in France over unrest
item.description: Police arrested 1,314 people in weekend protests across France, the interior ministry said Sunday, adding that 53 officers were hurt in clashes. The arrests occurred as violence broke out on the margins of mass demonstrations in major cities on Saturday over the high cost of living. It was the second consecutive weekend of unrest in France, which is heading to presidential elections in April and May to choose a successor to Emmanuel Macron, who is reaching his two-term limit. The interior ministry said police responded to 75 fires during Saturday’s protests, adding that 24 shops were looted. “Several investigations have been opened,” it said in a statement, without giving details. It said that the rest of Saturday night, after the clashes had died down, was “calm”. The ministry statement on Sunday did not say how many protesters were hurt. Late Saturday, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez spoke of two serious injuries among protesters: one in Toulouse and one in Clermont-Ferrand. – Protesters hurt – The Toulouse prefecture, which reports to the interior ministry, told AFP that a 20-year-old man was seriously hurt with a wound to his hand. A street medic who tended demonstrators told AFP, on condition of anonymity, that the man had “several fingers” blown off his right hand. The prefecture covering Clermont-Ferrand said a man there also had a hand hurt, but did not suffer the loss of any fingers. A French regional daily, La Nouvelle Republique, reported that a man in Poitiers was hurt in his left eye, showing a photo of a man holding his face. The newspaper’s photographer told AFP he was a 19-year-old who was wounded during a charge by riot police firing stun grenades and tear gas. There have been several instances in recent weeks, during student protests in France, of people being maimed by police stun grenades or tear gas grenades. It was not known if the injuries reported from Saturday were from those police weapons. item.title: Mother, child die as two container trucks overturn in Lagos
item.description: By Efe Onodjae A mother and her child have died after two heavily laden 20-foot container trucks overturned at Mile 2, near Freeman Market, inward Apapa, Lagos. The victims were trapped beneath the overturned trucks and their containers during the incident, which occurred over the weekend. The Lagos State Traffic Management Authority, LASTMA, said its rescue and recovery personnel responded to the scene to evacuate the victims and remove the wreckage. According to the agency, the road was temporarily cordoned off, while traffic was diverted through an adjoining service lane to ease congestion and prevent further accidents. LASTMA deployed a crane and a high-capacity tow vehicle to remove the overturned trucks and their cargoes, while officers of the Nigeria Police Force provided security during the operation. The remains of the victims were subsequently conveyed to the police mortuary in Yaba for necessary procedures. The General Manager of LASTMA, Mr Olalekan Bakare-Oki, expressed sadness over the incident and called for a thorough investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the accident. He urged relevant security agencies to determine whether mechanical defects, excessive loading, improper cargo distribution, driver negligence or other factors contributed to the incident. Bakare-Oki also called on truck operators to ensure their vehicles were roadworthy, secure their cargoes properly and comply with established road safety regulations. item.title: Troops neutralise 6 terrorists, arrest 11 suspected collaborators in Borno
item.description: Troops of the Nigerian Army have neutralised six terrorists, arrested 11 suspected collaborators and received the surrender of a Jama’atu Ahlis Sunna Lidda’awati wal-Jihad (JAS) member in Borno. This is contained in an operational report made available to the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN), on Sunday in Abuja. The report said the operations, conducted by troops of the Joint Task Force North-East, Operation Hadin Kai (OPHK), targeted terrorist fighters and suspected support networks in Kaga and Gwoza Local Government Areas. It said troops of 29 Task Force Brigade Garrison, supported by Hybrid Force personnel, ambushed suspected Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP)/JAS terrorists along the Targejeri axis of Kaga at about 12:37 a.m. on Oct. 25. According to the report, six terrorists were neutralised during the encounter, while troops recovered an AK-47 rifle, three magazines and 169 rounds of 7.62mm special ammunition. “Other recovered items included two Android phones, three button phones and charms. “In a related development, troops arrested six additional suspected terrorist collaborators during a follow-up raid in Benisheikh, Kaga, at about 6:20 a.m. on Oct. 24. “The arrests brought the number of suspects apprehended in connection with the investigation to 11, including five earlier arrests. “Items listed as recovered during the raid included an AK-47 rifle, three empty magazines, 169 rounds of 7.62mm special ammunition, three terrorist uniforms, a turban, a head mask, two Android phones, three button phones and charms,” it said. The report said the suspects were undergoing investigation to establish their alleged involvement in terrorist activities and identify possible links to other members of the network. It added that troops of 192 Battalion (Main), supported by Hybrid Force personnel at Hambagda Internally Displaced Persons (IDP) Camp in Gwoza, received a JAS member who surrendered at about 9:20 p.m. on Saturday. According to the report, preliminary investigation indicated that the individual had escaped from a terrorist enclave in the Mandara Mountains area of Gwoza and decided to abandon terrorism. “The individual surrendered with an AK-47 rifle and a magazine containing 28 rounds of 7.62mm special ammunition,” it added. The report said the defector was in custody undergoing further investigation and processing in line with established procedures. It said the operations underscore OPHK’s continued efforts to disrupt terrorist activities, dismantle support networks and encourage defections through sustained, intelligence-led operations. The military urged members of the public to provide credible and timely information to security agencies to support efforts to restore peace and enable displaced communities to return safely. item.title: What happens at a polling unit? A step-by-step guide to voting in Nigeria
item.description: Sekinat Osundiji A polling unit is where voters go to cast their ballots during an election. It is also where election officials verify voters’ identities, issue ballot papers, and count votes after voting ends. For many Nigerians, understanding what happens at a polling unit can help them prepare for election day and know what to expect when they arrive to vote. Here is how the process works. Voters arrive at their polling units On election day, registered voters go to the polling units where their names appear on the voters’ register. item.content:encoded: Sekinat Osundiji A polling unit is where voters go to cast their ballots during an election. It is also where election officials verify voters’ identities, issue ballot papers, and count votes after voting ends. For many Nigerians, understanding what happens at a polling unit can help them prepare for election day and know what to expect when they arrive to vote. Here is how the process works. Voters arrive at their polling units On election day, registered voters go to the polling units where their names appear on the voters’ register. They are expected to check their polling unit before leaving home to avoid going to the wrong location. At the polling unit, officials organise voters and direct them to the appropriate queues. Security personnel may also be present to maintain order and prevent disruptions. Election officials verify voters Before voting, officials check the voters’ register to confirm that each person is registered at that polling unit. The voter’s identity is then verified using the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS), which is used by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) for voter accreditation. The system checks the voter’s details and may use fingerprint or facial recognition, depending on the circumstances. If accreditation is unsuccessful, officials follow INEC’s prescribed procedures. Only voters who meet the accreditation requirements are allowed to proceed to vote. Voters receive their ballot papers After accreditation, election officials issue ballot papers for the elections taking place. Depending on the election, voters may receive separate ballot papers for positions such as president, governor, senator or member of the House of Representatives. Officials explain how to mark the ballot correctly. Voters must follow the instructions to ensure their choices are properly recorded. Voters mark their choices in private Voters proceed to the designated voting area, where they mark their ballot papers in secret. They select their preferred candidate or party by following the instructions printed on the ballot paper. Maintaining secrecy is important because no one should be forced to reveal their vote or told whom to support. After marking the ballot, the voter folds it as directed and places it in the appropriate ballot box. Voting closes and votes are counted When voting ends, officials follow INEC’s procedures for closing the poll. At the polling unit, ballot papers are sorted and counted in the presence of authorised party agents, observers and other permitted persons. The votes are counted according to the candidates or parties they represent. Officials also account for rejected ballots, which are ballot papers that cannot be counted as valid votes under the applicable rules. The counting process is expected to be transparent, allowing those present to observe and raise concerns through the proper channels. Results are announced at the polling unit After counting, the presiding officer records the results on the prescribed result sheet. The results are announced at the polling unit, and party agents and other authorised persons can observe the process. Where applicable, the results are uploaded electronically through INEC’s designated result-transmission system. The polling-unit result is then taken through the appropriate collation process, where results from different polling units are combined at higher levels. The result announced at one polling unit does not, by itself, determine the overall winner of the election. What can voters do if something goes wrong? Party agents and accredited observers may document incidents and report them through the relevant channels. Voters should avoid violence, intimidation or actions that could disrupt the process. item.title: NDC to unveil campaign council, present financial statement at NEC meeting
item.description: The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) says it will unveil its National Campaign Council and present its statement of account at its third National Executive Committee (NEC) meeting scheduled for Monday, October 26, in Abuja. The party said the presentation of its financial statement was part of its commitment to transparency and accountability, challenging other political parties, particularly the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), to disclose details of their finances. The announcement was contained in a statement signed by the NDC National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, Esq. According to the statement, the meeting will hold at JD Event Centre, Kashim Ibrahim Way, opposite A-Class Park, Maitama, Abuja, at 10am. “A major highlight of the meeting will be the release and presentation of the party’s Statement of Account by the National Treasurer. This is in deference to our avowed commitment to the principles of transparency and accountability,” the statement said. The party challenged the APC and other political parties to follow its example in the management and disclosure of their finances. “In this regard, we challenge other political parties, especially the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), to emulate this level of openness and transparency in the management of their finances,” it added. The NDC also addressed speculation about its finances, saying its resources would have been more substantial but for the inability of many of its candidates to pay for nomination forms. The party attributed the situation to the economic hardship in the country, claiming that about 80 per cent of its candidates could not afford the expression of interest forms. “However, contrary to speculations in the public domain, and due to the level of poverty, hunger and deprivation in the country occasioned by the rudderless APC and its amorphous economic policies, about 80% of our candidates could not afford the Expression of Interest forms,” the statement said. It added that the party issued the forms free of charge to the affected candidates. The NDC further disclosed that the meeting would feature the unveiling of its National Campaign Council (NCC), which it said would cover campaigns for the presidential, National Assembly, governorship and state Houses of Assembly elections. The party also said its candidates would receive certificates of return for their respective offices. Describing itself as prepared for the 2027 general election, the NDC said it was determined to offer Nigerians what it called altruistic leadership. “The NDC is turbo-charged and ready to give Nigerians the altruistic leadership the nation deserves,” the statement said. item.title: Troops raid bandits enclave, rescue three kidnap victims in Kebbi
item.description: By Haruna Aliyu,Birnin Kebbi Troops of Sector 2, Operation Fansan Yamma, have rescued three kidnapped victims during an operation in Sakaba Local Government Area of Kebbi State. The victims were identified as Aisha Aminu, 46; Sumayya Aminu, 27; and Nana Abbas, 15. The rescue operation took place on Saturday, October 24, 2026, with two of the victims rescued at Makuku Village and the third at Dankolo Village. The development was disclosed in a statement made available to our correspondent on Sunday by the spokesman for the 8 Division, Nigerian Army, Lt. Col. Olaniyi Osoba. According to the statement, the operation was successfully concluded without any incident. “The victims were subsequently handed over to the District Head of Dirindaji, Alhaji Usman Muhammad, through the Chairman of Sakaba Local Government Area,” the statement said. The military described the operation as successful, noting that the rescued victims were transferred to the relevant local authorities after their recovery. “The operation was concluded successfully without any incident,” the statement added. Osoba reaffirmed the troops’ commitment to protecting residents and communities in the state, stressing that troops remained focused on their responsibility to safeguard lives and property. “Troops remain committed to the protection of lives and property,” the statement said. The rescue comes amid persistent security concerns in parts of Nigeria’s North-West, where kidnapping and other criminal activities have continued to threaten residents and disrupt community life. item.title: 2027: Sowore slams NDC, accuses Obi of renting party every election
item.description: The presidential candidate of the African Action Congress (AAC), Omoyele Sowore, has criticised the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) and accused its presidential candidate Peter Obi of renting political parties during election seasons. Sowore alleged that Obi’s political moves were not aimed at liberating Nigerians but at helping the ruling establishment deflect public anger and avoid accountability ahead of the 2027 general election. In a statement posted on X, Sowore accused the NDC of exploiting the political process, claiming that its leaders made ₦9 billion from the sale of nomination forms while running the party from their homes. “The same opportunists and packaged political frauds who made ₦9 billion from selling nomination forms while running a political party from their living rooms,” Sowore wrote, referring to the NDC. He described Obi as an unprincipled politician who, according to him, changes political platforms ahead of elections without offering a genuine challenge to the political establishment. “This is the problem with unprincipled politicians like Peter Obi, who rent political parties every election season, not to liberate Nigerians, but to…. divert public anger and evade the revolutionary consequences of their actions,” he said. Sowore also accused supporters of Obi and other political figures of attempting to discredit critics and distract Nigerians from what he described as the country’s underlying social and political problems. He named Osun State Governor Ademola Adeleke and Abia State Governor Alex Otti among those he alleged had helped promote narratives that distract from these issues. “But we cannot be fooled,” Sowore said, insisting that the politicians he criticised were delaying what he described as the liberation of Nigerians. The AAC candidate further alleged that Obi and his allies were not genuinely opposed to Tinubu’s administration but were instead seeking to manage opposition to the president without mounting a strong challenge to his government. “They don’t oppose Tinubu; they simply don’t want anyone to oppose him strongly enough to bring his disastrous reign to an end. Their politics is about managing opposition, not confronting the system,” he said. Sowore also referred to a remark attributed to Datti Baba-Ahmed, Obi’s former running mate in the 2023 presidential election, describing Tinubu as their “favourite uncle”. Obi, who contested the 2023 presidential election on the platform of the Labour Party, has since moved to the NDC ahead of the 2027 election. item.title: Obama blasts Trump’s ‘chaos and cruelty’ while campaigning for Democrats
item.description: Former US president Barack Obama delivered scathing criticisms of his successor, Donald Trump, at rallies Saturday in Ohio and Michigan to support Democratic candidates ahead of the November 3 midterm elections. Democrats are attempting to wrest back control of one or both chambers of the US Congress, which are currently controlled by Trump’s Republican party. The former president retains considerable popularity among the Democratic base, which he is keen to leverage to support his Democratic Party’s candidates. In both states, the 65-year-old former president blamed the Trump administration for the rising cost of living, a top voter concern amid soaring fuel prices. “The current president chose to make a series of bad decisions,” Obama said in Ohio, where he rallied in support of former Democratic senator Sherrod Brown. “Most importantly, he decided to start an unnecessary war that nobody asked for.” “After two years of chaos and cruelty and corruption and incompetence, the likes of which we have not seen in the modern era, you get a chance to say, ‘Enough is enough,'” Obama declared in Cleveland. “We are voting for change right here in Ohio.” Later, in Michigan, Obama campaigned for Abdul El-Sayed, from the party’s left wing, who is in a close race with Republican Mike Rogers for the US Senate. “Imagine the power duo of Abdul and Elissa,” Obama said, referring to the incumbent Democratic Senator Elissa Slotkin, who is not up for election this year. “You got a Muslim man, you got a Jewish woman fighting for you in the United States Senate. That’s something, Michigan, you can be proud of.” Obama also urged voters to cast their ballots as soon as possible since early voting is already open in both states. “Don’t procrastinate, don’t equivocate,” Obama said. In Ohio, Brown will attempt a comeback against incumbent Republican Senator Jon Husted, while the race for governor will be contested between Democrat Amy Acton and Republican Vivek Ramaswamy, a former presidential candidate in 2024. Polls for Ohio give Democrats a slight lead in both those races, but the results are expected to be close. Obama also took digs at Trump’s renovation projects across the US capital, including his botched renovation of the National Mall’s Reflecting Pool, his construction of a massive White House Ballroom and the guilded decorations he has adorned the Oval Office with during his second tenure. “He’s got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory,” Obama said, referring to popular but indulgent American restaurant chain. item.title: My wife died two years ago, then grief opened door for madness
item.description: My Peju Akande Mywife died two years ago. Before then, she had been sick for a long time; the kind of sickness that drains everybody in the house. You know that saying: “The person caring for the sick is sometimes sicker than the sick person.” It’s true. It’s painfully true. I won’t stand here and claim I did all the caring. Her children, our children, carried that burden with full chest. They were her hands, her legs and her nurses. But she was still mywife. I did what I could, in my own small way. I put all my manhood on hold and accepted it as destiny. You know what I mean. When she died, the house became quiet in a way that frightens even an old man. There used to be noise, you know, the good kind. People trooping in and out. Neighbours, people from our mosque, alfas, children she helped, women she advised, men she encouraged. Big tree Mywife was a big tree. When she fell, the shade disappeared. People came for the burial, stayed for a while, then left one by one like leaves falling off a branch. And I was alone. My children begged me to come and stay with them, but grief is a stubborn companion. I said I wanted to be alone. I didn’t realise loneliness has teeth. Not that I feared ghosts, if mywife appeared, even as a ghost, she wouldn’t harm me. She would probably scold me for misplacing my glasses, or my phone or even money. Eventually, my children arranged someone to cook and clean. I was turning 80; I needed help. Even if it was someone to quarrel with. That’s how I met this woman at the mosque. The ‘eleha’ who hid her evil under a burqa. She was an eleha, fully covered, soft‑spoken, eyes lowered. But I was fooled in my old age! I’m not saying women who wear hijab or burqa are evil. No. But this particular one used that covering to hide her wickedness like a snake hiding under dry leaves. She was 45 when we met. She said her husband left her with three children. item.content:encoded: My Peju Akande Mywife died two years ago. Before then, she had been sick for a long time; the kind of sickness that drains everybody in the house. You know that saying: “The person caring for the sick is sometimes sicker than the sick person.” It’s true. It’s painfully true. I won’t stand here and claim I did all the caring. Her children, our children, carried that burden with full chest. They were her hands, her legs and her nurses. But she was still mywife. I did what I could, in my own small way. I put all my manhood on hold and accepted it as destiny. You know what I mean. When she died, the house became quiet in a way that frightens even an old man. There used to be noise, you know, the good kind. People trooping in and out. Neighbours, people from our mosque, alfas, children she helped, women she advised, men she encouraged.
